To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of domestic learning and foreign learning processes is the key to understand the M&A outflows of EMNE.

the combination of domestic and learning abroad processes, as a result of the use of M&A as a strategy of internationalisation by EMNE, is a positive factor for the generation of technological catch up in the NSI of the home country.
the use of M&A by emerging multinationals may be a result of interactive processes between domestic learning and learning from abroad.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact that the interaction between home country NSIs, and the internationalisation of firms from emerging economies has on the use of M&A as a strategy to overcome domestic weaknesses in less-advanced NSIs.
the role of NSIs in shaping the internationalisation strategies of EMNE.
the role of NSI characteristics in the internationalisation process of M&As, and the interactive learning processes that result from the link between M&A outflows and inward FDI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EMNEs from developing countries are not only able to acquire foreign firms in developed countries but also are able to generate a learning process in both directions, which in turn may be an important source for technological upgrading and economic growth in developing countries.
M&A activity is a relevant and important tool for EMNEs to acquire and exploit knowledge, and it is positively influenced by the quality of domestic and host NSIs.
EMNEs from developing economies have a greater propensity to acquire firms in advanced economies than to acquire firms in other developing economies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of M&A by firms from emerging countries is a strategic choice to compensate domestic weaknesses in less developed NSIs, which may be a result of the combination between domestic learning and learning in the home country.

M&A outflows are positively related to domestic technological catch up, but negatively to inward foreign direct investment, and that the relationship between domestic learning and learning from abroad is positive, but only in less advanced NSIs.
EMNEs may use their M&A outflow as a learning process to overcome the weaknesses of their home NSI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of both learning processes (domestic and abroad) is a key driver in explaining the use of M&A as a mode of internationalisation by EMNE.
the use of M&A by EMNE may be a strategic option to compensate for domestic weaknesses and reinforce the use of inward FDI as a mechanism of learning.
EMNEs may benefit from the interactive learning process that takes place when they invest in developed countries, and this is more relevant in less advanced NSIs.
